title: Famous laws of science
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: A scientific law is a short statement of something nature always does, tested again and again. These are the ones that turn up in every physics and chemistry class, and knowing who found them, and when, ties science to history.

How to hold it: Encode the meaning before the name: for each law, picture the everyday scene in the hook and say the law in your own words (narration). Then hang it on a timeline, chunked by century, so the people line up in order: Archimedes alone in the ancient world, then Kepler, Boyle, Hooke and Newton in the 1600s, and so on. Retrieve it by explaining one law a day to someone else.
This list has 22 items. Answer below, then check — the practice button generates fresh questions from the list itself.
